question.:question/problem:
Solve the differential equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=6 \cos{\left(2 x \right)}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation once, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(6 \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\  & =((6)\int \left(\cos{\left(2 x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =((6)\left(\frac{\sin{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}\right))+C \\  & =C + 3 \sin{\left(2 x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(C + 3 \sin{\left(2 x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =((3)\int \left(\sin{\left(2 x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x)+C\int \text{d}x \\  & =((3)\left(- \frac{\cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}\right))+Cx+D \\  & =C x + D - \frac{3 \cos{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because we had a second-order equation, our general solution contains *two* arbitrary constants, $C$ and $D.$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the General Solution of a Second Order Differential Equation by Integrating Twice

question.:question/problem:
Solve the differential equation

$$
3\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=24 x^{4} + 24 x^{3} - 6 \sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to give

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=8 x^{4} + 8 x^{3} - 2 \sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}.
$$

Now, integrating the equation once, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(8 x^{4} + 8 x^{3} - 2 \sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\  & =((8)\int \left(x^{3}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((8)\int \left(x^{4}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((-2)\int \left(\sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =((8)\left(\frac{x^{4}}{4}\right)) + ((8)\left(\frac{x^{5}}{5}\right)) + ((-2)\left(- 2 \cos{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right))+C \\  & =C + \frac{8 x^{5}}{5} + 2 x^{4} + 4 \cos{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(C + \frac{8 x^{5}}{5} + 2 x^{4} + 4 \cos{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =((2)\int \left(x^{4}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((\frac{8}{5})\int \left(x^{5}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((4)\int \left(\cos{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x)+C\int \text{d}x \\  & =((2)\left(\frac{x^{5}}{5}\right)) + ((\frac{8}{5})\left(\frac{x^{6}}{6}\right)) + ((4)\left(2 \sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}\right))+Cx+D \\  & =C x + D + \frac{4 x^{6}}{15} + \frac{2 x^{5}}{5} + 8 \sin{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because we had a second-order equation, our general solution contains *two* arbitrary constants, $C$ and $D.$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the General Solution of a Second Order Differential Equation by Integrating Twice

question.:question/problem:
Solve the differential equation

$$
2\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=4 \cdot 4^{x} + 12 x^{2} + 8 \cos{\left(x \right)}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to give

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=2 \cdot 4^{x} + 6 x^{2} + 4 \cos{\left(x \right)}.
$$

Now, integrating the equation once, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(2 \cdot 4^{x} + 6 x^{2} + 4 \cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\  & =((6)\int \left(x^{2}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((2)\int \left(4^{x}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((4)\int \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =((6)\left(\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right)) + ((2)\left(\frac{4^{x}}{2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)) + ((4)\left(\sin{\left(x \right)}\right))+C \\  & =\frac{4^{x}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}} + C + 2 x^{3} + 4 \sin{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(\frac{4^{x}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}} + C + 2 x^{3} + 4 \sin{\left(x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =((2)\int \left(x^{3}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}})\int \left(4^{x}\right)\,\text{d}x) + ((4)\int \left(\sin{\left(x \right)}\right)\,\text{d}x)+C\int \text{d}x \\  & =((2)\left(\frac{x^{4}}{4}\right)) + ((\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}})\left(\frac{4^{x}}{2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)) + ((4)\left(- \cos{\left(x \right)}\right))+Cx+D \\  & =\frac{2^{2 x - 1}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}^{2}} + C x + D + \frac{x^{4}}{2} - 4 \cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because we had a second-order equation, our general solution contains *two* arbitrary constants, $C$ and $D.$
